**Visa upgrades account-to-account fraud protection with Featurespace AI**

*Enhanced fraud interception for credit transfers across Europe arrives as instant payments volumes and account-to-account adoption continue to climb.*

Visa is integrating Featurespace's machine learning technology into its account-to-account (A2A) Protect product, giving banks the ability to detect and block fraudulent credit transfers before funds leave the sender's account. The upgrade targets the growing fraud exposure created by rising instant payment volumes, where speed of settlement leaves little room for manual intervention.

A2A Protect launched as Visa's answer to the fraud risks inherent in real-time account-to-account payments – a segment where the company has less natural presence than in card-based transactions. Adding Featurespace's adaptive behavioural analytics sharpens the product's real-time scoring, positioning it against bank-built and third-party fraud engines already operating in this space.

European banks face mounting pressure on multiple fronts: the SEPA instant payments regulation demands broader reach, verification-of-payee requirements remain unevenly implemented, and authorised push payment fraud losses in the UK reached £576.4 million in 2024. Visa's move reflects a broader pattern of card networks building defensive infrastructure around account-to-account rails they do not own but increasingly need to service.

*Sources: [Visa Enhances A2A Protect with Featurespace Tech to Combat Account-to-Account Fraud](https://ffnews.com/news/news-visa-launches-enhanced-a2a-protect-to-stop-fraud-before-money-leaves-accoun-b3f93d50) — Ffnews*

**Reserve Bank of Australia rules out retail central bank digital currency**

*Australia's removal from the diminishing list of advanced economies actively pursuing a retail CBDC reinforces the divergence between Europe's digital euro programme and the scepticism building elsewhere.*

The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) has concluded that there is no clear public interest case for issuing a retail central bank digital currency (CBDC), finding that existing payment systems serve households adequately. The decision follows several years of research and pilot work, and effectively closes the door on an Australian retail CBDC for the foreseeable future.

Australia joins a growing cohort of central banks – including the US Federal Reserve and, more recently, the Bank of Canada – that have stepped back from retail CBDC issuance. The contrast with the European Central Bank is stark: the ECB selected 36 payment providers for its digital euro pilot phase and the European Parliament voted to advance the digital euro regulation to final negotiations.

The RBA's reasoning matters as much as the conclusion. The finding that existing infrastructure is sufficient echoes arguments made by private-sector critics of the digital euro, who contend that Europe's challenge is one of payments fragmentation and sovereignty rather than a gap that only a CBDC can fill. Each major economy that declines to issue a retail CBDC strengthens the hand of those arguing the digital euro solves a problem that could be addressed by other means.

*Sources: [RBA concludes no case for retail CBDC in Australia](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48343/rba-concludes-no-case-for-retail-cbdc-in-australia?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**OpenPayd secures US state licences as it prepares American market entry**

*The London-based embedded finance provider has acquired 43 state money transmitter licences, adding a US footprint as it also pursues a Nasdaq listing via SPAC.*

Securing money transmitter licences across 43 states gives OpenPayd a regulated basis to offer its payment infrastructure to American clients, complementing the embedded finance and stablecoin services provider's existing European operations.

The US push follows OpenPayd's announcement in March that it is pursuing a Nasdaq listing through a $1.145 billion SPAC deal. European payments infrastructure firms have historically struggled to gain traction in the US against entrenched domestic players. OpenPayd's stablecoin capabilities, including its recent connection to Circle's network for stablecoin-settled fiat payouts, give it a differentiated proposition in a US market where stablecoin regulation is advancing rapidly under new federal legislation.

Several large global banks have committed to a joint stablecoin venture with a euro-denominated token as a priority. OpenPayd's ability to operate across both traditional fiat rails and stablecoin infrastructure positions it at the intersection of these two trends, though building meaningful US market share from a European base remains a formidable challenge.

*Sources: [OpenPayd Prepares for a U.S. Launch As Big Banks Plan for a Dollar Stablecoin](https://www.digitaltransactions.net/openpayd-prepares-for-a-u-s-launch-as-big-banks-plan-for-a-dollar-stablecoin/) — Digitaltransactions*

**ACI Worldwide acquires Cranium Ventures for cloud-native card switching**

*Microservices-based card payment switching fills a gap in ACI's stack as the company balances its growing instant payments business with core card infrastructure modernisation.*

ACI Worldwide has agreed to acquire Cranium Ventures, a developer of cloud-native card payment switching technology. Financial terms were not disclosed. The acquisition brings microservices architecture into ACI's card processing capabilities, addressing a technology gap as banks and processors increasingly demand modular, cloud-deployed infrastructure.

ACI has been on an active acquisition and partnership path this year. It was selected to process instant payments for the European Payments Initiative across Europe and has been exploring a sale of its billing division. Cranium's switching technology extends ACI's investment in its card processing business, even as the company builds out its real-time payments portfolio.

Cloud-native card switching is a competitive space. Legacy switching platforms, many built on monolithic architectures, are expensive to maintain and slow to adapt. Processors that can offer banks modular, API-driven switching alongside instant payment capabilities are better positioned as European banks simultaneously modernise card infrastructure and comply with instant payments mandates.

*Sources: [ACI Worldwide to add microservices card switching via Cranium Ventures acquisition](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48339/aci-worldwide-to-add-microservices-card-switching-via-cranium-ventures-acquisition?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*
